body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat V_\star\text{ total computable with }\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,K}}E_{P^n}[(\widehat V_\star-V^\star(P))^2]\asymp R(n,d,K)\asymp r_\star(n,d,K)\)

sampling_model.design: Observational i.i.d. sampling from an unknown law in \(\mathcal M_{d,K}\).
sampling_model.treatment: \(A_i\in[K]\) is logged with unknown \(e_{ax}\) satisfying only \(e_{ax}\ge1/(2K)\) on positive-mass groups; the simplex constraint permits propensities larger than \(2/K\).
sampling_model.overlap: Menu-scaled lower overlap is imposed only on \(x\) with \(p_x>0\); null groups and unobserved sample cells are legal.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The upper bound must estimate or avoid both unknown \(p_x\) and unknown \(e_{ax}\); known-uniform subexperiments may be used only for the converse.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: HAVER uses a lower-confidence pivot and head averaging to obtain instance-dependent MSE upper bounds for passive maximum-mean estimation.
Theorem 7 proves that a \(1/14\)-uniform approximation to Boolean OR has degree at least \(\sqrt K\).
The paper characterizes pathwise differentiability of optimal value and gives online one-step inference under fixed-complexity asymptotics.

The static optimal-value theorem proves asymptotic linearity, and asymptotic normality when the influence variance is positive, for an independent-sample de-biased softmax estimator under \(\delta\)-polynomial suboptimality-gap density, \(\beta_n=\omega(n^{1/[2(1+\delta)]})\), stated \(L^2\) nuisance convergence and product-rate conditions, and uniform boundedness.
The paper combines smooth--nonsmooth splitting, polynomial approximation, factorial moments, and fuzzy hypotheses for additive discrete-distribution functionals.
The paper uses best-polynomial and moment-matching duality to derive the all-regime entropy MSE and its consistency threshold.
The paper proves multi-action policy-regret bounds over restricted policy classes using doubly robust scores.

body.tldr: A growing treatment menu turns each sparse patient group into a high-dimensional nonsmooth maximum with random denominators. The headline kernel is the explicit all-regime minimax MSE \(r_\star(n,d,K)\), with a total statistically computable estimator on the full unknown-mass class under menu-scaled lower overlap alone and a matching same-class converse. The mathematical hinge is a dimension-uniform certificate that makes maximum-approximation bias, exact factorial-lift covariance, and normalized moment-prior mixture geometry share one evaluated scale, while exposing the finite coefficient count \(M_{2K,L}=\binom{2K+L}{L}\) and the estimator's combinatorial evaluation cost. Supporting claims cover the one-group and \(K\ge d^2\) rates and a new binary-to-many-arm hardness transfer; the accepted \(K=2\) frontier is used only as a cited boundary condition. The open content is the exact transition for \(2<K<d^2\) and the resulting necessary-and-sufficient consistency boundary.

project_justification.gap: The literature separates fixed-dimensional nonregular inference, restricted-class policy regret, one-group maximum-mean upper bounds, and scalar approximation-theoretic minimax estimation; none gives the joint finite-sample risk when sparse categorical groups and treatments grow together under unknown observational logging and only a menu-scaled lower propensity bound.
project_justification.niche: The categorical experiment has exact Poisson factorial and likelihood-mixture identities, but its \(K\)-way tie fan, arbitrary group occupancy, and potentially unbalanced logging require a dimension-uniform primal--dual certificate with an explicit finite representation.
project_justification.fill: The project evaluates that certificate, splices it to the supporting one-group and many-arm results, the new binary-grouping transfer, and the cited \(K=2\) boundary, then turns the closed-form envelope into a total computable estimator, an all-estimator lower bound, and exact consistency and parametric-MSE conditions.

body.related_work: LuedtkeVanderLaan2016 supplies the standard identification and nonregularity boundary: its pathwise-differentiability theorem and online estimator explain why exact ties defeat ordinary first-order inference, but identification is not an originality target here and the paper does not address growing-dimensional minimax MSE. WhitehouseAusternSyrgkanis2025 is an informed-by comparison rather than a theorem target. Its static theorem assumes independent evaluation data; a \(\delta\)-polynomial density for every suboptimality gap, allowing an atom at zero; \(\beta_n=\omega(n^{1/[2(1+\delta)]})\); \(\lVert\widehat Q_n-Q^\star\rVert_2=o_P(n^{-1/4}\beta_n^{-1/2})\); a product nuisance error of \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\); \(L^2\) consistency; uniform boundedness; and positive influence variance for the normal limit. The unrestricted finite-sample class here assumes none of the density or nuisance-rate conditions and permits both dimensions to grow. NguyenBarrettJun2025HAVER is the closest estimator comparator: its lower-confidence pivot and head averaging control passive one-group MSE, but random patient-group counts, unknown masses, causal logging, and a global converse are absent. JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015 supplies the nonsmooth--smooth split, factorial-moment lift, clipping, and fuzzy-hypothesis architecture. WuYang2016 supplies the stronger requirement that approximation and moment-matched priors be governed by the same extremal quantity, including an evaluated consistency threshold. CaiLow2011 supplies the moment-prior and chi-square template for a kinked functional. Spalek2008 is the obstruction comparator: its explicit dual polynomial shows that a uniform maximum surrogate cannot hide \(K\) in its degree. LuedtkeVanderLaan2018 studies maxima with a possibly growing index set under asymptotic remainder conditions, not sparse-table all-regime risk. ZhouAtheyWager2023 concerns learned-policy regret over restricted classes and motivates lower overlap, but it is a consumer-facing neighbor rather than a theorem-level target.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The early Boolean check for \(K=64\) gives numerical best errors approximately \(0.784421\), \(0.500867\), and \(0.412390\) at degrees \(4\), \(7\), and \(8\), respectively. These floating-point linear programs are reconnaissance only. The rigorous content is the OR obstruction in \(\mathrm{lem{:}or\text{-}obstruction}\) and the exact lifted-variance identity in \(\mathrm{lem{:}poisson\text{-}lift\text{-}identity}\). A degree-\(L\) local lift has \(M_{2K,L}=\binom{2K+L}{L}\) coefficients in the full observed-cell representation, so the displayed evaluation routine is finite but may be exponential in \(K\) or \(L\). No polynomial-time theorem is claimed, and a proposed solution that suppresses this dependence fails the kernel.
body.honest_scope: The full joint rate \(r_\star(n,d,K)\), the attaining estimator \(\widehat V_\star\), and the exact consistency boundary are open objects isolated in \(\mathrm{oeq{:}joint\text{-}frontier}\). The proof obligations retained in the core are the lower-overlap full-class empirical upper bound, the centered-winner lower envelope, the matched region \(K\ge d^2\), the one-group benchmark, and the binary-to-many-arm transfer. The accepted \(K=2\) frontier and standard causal identification are cited boundary conditions, not originality or solve targets. Total statistical computability is required through a finite coefficient table, exact certificate generation, and the displayed dense evaluation bound; polynomial-time computation is not claimed. The paper does not claim inference for a learned policy, a budget curve, sharp leading constants, or honest confidence intervals. The \(d=2,K=3\) witness verifies that unequal logging and switching maximizing arms remain inside the enlarged lower-overlap-only class.
